text: Twenty percent of the world's oil passes through a channel just twenty one miles wide. That map, that chart, and this whole video were made from one sentence, by MitraField.

Explainer videos are how people learn. But making a correct one takes days. And text to video tools hallucinate. They invent coastlines and garble numbers. For learning, a wrong number is worse than none.
With MitraField, you just ask. Type a question, pick a landscape video or a vertical short, choose a language and a narrator, and add your notes or a PDF as the source of truth.

A Gemini director agent writes the story beat by beat, and sends each beat to the engine that can show it truthfully. Facts, maps and math go to exact engines drawn by code. Mood and metaphor go to Nano Banana and Veo.

The director also defines the cast. The style, the guide character, and the ship itself. Each gets one reference image, so the Titanic looks the same in every still, and Veo animates it from an on model first frame.
There are ten engines. Gemini writes Manim code, renders it, and checks the frames. The globe uses real Natural Earth borders. Charts, timelines and flow diagrams are computed, never imagined.
Every beat is editable. Change a line, swap an engine, or just tell the director: show it on a map. Only that beat renders again.
Each finished video comes with music, subtitles and a cost meter. A fifty second short costs about two dollars and renders in a few minutes, with no manual editing.
Gemini, Nano Banana, Veo, Gemini text to speech and Lyria, working as one director. MitraField. Explain it once. Every beat finds its engine.
